paragraphs.text: A museum in a northern city holds no objects at all. Its collection is sound: three thousand recordings of workplaces, streets and machines, some of which no longer exist anywhere.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Recording is harder than it looks. A microphone in a workshop picks up the ventilation as loudly as the lathe, and curators often return three or four times before a recording is usable.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Visitors listen in small dark rooms, with one recording each, and the museum reports that people stay far longer than in a room of photographs of the same workplaces.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: The archive is also used by people who cannot visit. Film-makers licence the recordings, and one hospital plays them to patients who grew up in the district.
paragraphs.label: D

groups.instruction: Questions 1–4. The text has 4 paragraphs, A–D. Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below.
